The api was to include the "basic" accessors before deciding on more high level (higher load) requirements for the BN I think we could make a strong case for including it in the canonical api. excerpts.author: paulhauner
excerpts.content:
Hey 🙂 When it comes to the `justified` and `finalized` IDs in `../beacon/states/...`, it seems there's two potential options if the epoch-boundary state for that epoch is a skip slot:

- The state of the block which corresponds to the finalized block root (`state.slot != start_slot(finalized_epoch)`)
- The "skip state" so that `state.slot == start_slot(finalized_epoch)`

I'm wondering if someone has someone across this before?

excerpts.author: djrtwo
excerpts.content: Id assume almost certainly the skip slots included in the transition because thats what is actually finalized

excerpts.author: paulhauner
excerpts.content:
> Id assume almost certainly the skip slots included in the transition because thats what is actually finalized
<@!291925846556540928> To me, this makes the most sense for a user. Unfortunately it naively makes our lookups `O(slots_since_head)` instead of `O(1)`, but I think it'll be fine.

excerpts.author: djrtwo
excerpts.content:
I would have assumed justified and finalized state were very cheap

Why do you have the state at the block rather than the finalized state?

excerpts.author: paulhauner
excerpts.content:
> Why do you have the state at the block rather than the finalized state?
Beacuse then you get `get_state(get_block(head_state.finalized_checkpoint.root).state_root)`

excerpts.author: paulhauner
excerpts.content: Instead of iterating backwards through `head_state.state_roots`, searching for the one at slot `start_slot(head_state.finalized_checkpoint.epoch)`

excerpts.author: djrtwo
excerpts.content: I see

excerpts.author: paulhauner
excerpts.content:
> - The "skip state" so that state.slot == start_slot(finalized_epoch)
I've just implemented it so we return this state 🙂
